headline: Fuel prices rise up to nearly 36% between January and September 2026
summary: The hike has sparked widespread anger among passengers and drivers, with experts warning of a ripple effect across the economy and production costs.
details: Fuel prices in Bangladesh have surged by nearly 36% between January and September 2026, triggering widespread public anger and anxiety.
The price hike has already disrupted public transport in Chittagong and sparked protests by political parties including Jamaat-e-Islami and the NCP.
Transport operators are proposing fare hikes for long-distance and city buses to offset the costs, while truck rental fees have already increased.

Economists and experts warn that higher fuel prices will push up production costs and create a ripple effect across the entire economy, specifically impacting the price of vegetables and other essential goods.
The government is reportedly bearing a loss of Tk 70 per litre of diesel, despite the recent price increases, according to official sources.
Some political leaders and experts have called for the cutting of fuel import taxes to mitigate the impact on the general public.
caption:
Fuel prices jumped nearly 36% in just nine months. The ripple effect is already hitting transport and food prices.

Fuel prices in Bangladesh have surged by nearly 36% between January and September 2026, triggering widespread public anger and anxiety.

The price hike has already disrupted public transport in Chittagong and sparked protests by political parties including Jamaat-e-Islami and the NCP.

Transport operators are proposing fare hikes for long-distance and city buses to offset the costs, while truck rental fees have already increased.

Economists and experts warn that higher fuel prices will push up production costs and create a ripple effect across the entire economy, specifically impacting the price of vegetables and other essential goods.

The government is reportedly bearing a loss of Tk 70 per litre of diesel, despite the recent price increases, according to official sources.

Some political leaders and experts have called for the cutting of fuel import taxes to mitigate the impact on the general public.

headline_marked: MP Gazi Nazrul [[placed on 4-day remand]] over 2nd wife's death
headline: MP Gazi Nazrul placed on 4-day remand over 2nd wife's death
summary: The lawmaker and his first wife are accused of abetting the suicide of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun following allegations of physical and mental abuse.
details: A Dhaka court has placed Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam on a four-day remand and his first wife, Maksuda Begum, on a one-day remand.
The action follows a case filed over the alleged abetment of the suicide of the lawmaker's second wife, 19-year-old Mariam Khatun, who was found hanging in a flat opposite the Jatiya Sangsad.
Mariam's father, SM Masum Billah, filed the case alleging that Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda physically and mentally abused the teenager, who had previously informed her family of the abuse over the phone.
Gazi Nazrul has denied the allegations, stating he was not at home during the incident and that Mariam took her own life.
The case also names Mariam's maternal uncle and the lawmaker's driver, Obaidur Rahman, as accused parties.

The death comes amid recent controversy involving the lawmaker, including the circulation of intimate video clips on social media and his expulsion from the Jamaat-e-Islami party for moral misconduct.
Local BNP and Jamaat leaders, as well as citizens' forums in Shyamnagar, have demanded a neutral investigation and exemplary punishment for those responsible.
caption:
An MP and his first wife are in remand after his 19-year-old second wife was found dead by suicide.

A Dhaka court has placed Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam on a four-day remand and his first wife, Maksuda Begum, on a one-day remand.

The action follows a case filed over the alleged abetment of the suicide of the lawmaker's second wife, 19-year-old Mariam Khatun, who was found hanging in a flat opposite the Jatiya Sangsad.

Mariam's father, SM Masum Billah, filed the case alleging that Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda physically and mentally abused the teenager, who had previously informed her family of the abuse over the phone.

Gazi Nazrul has denied the allegations, stating he was not at home during the incident and that Mariam took her own life.

The case also names Mariam's maternal uncle and the lawmaker's driver, Obaidur Rahman, as accused parties.

The death comes amid recent controversy involving the lawmaker, including the circulation of intimate video clips on social media and his expulsion from the Jamaat-e-Islami party for moral misconduct.

Local BNP and Jamaat leaders, as well as citizens' forums in Shyamnagar, have demanded a neutral investigation and exemplary punishment for those responsible.
